why: AI reviewers are good at comparing projects but poor at absolute scores: they hedge toward the middle. In LetsVibe's own testing, a deliberately terrible app and a carefully built one, graded by the same pipeline, averaged about 28 and 68 on a 0-100 scale, and repeated runs of the same project varied by several points. A raw score therefore says little on its own, so LetsVibe grades on a bell curve: what counts is how your project compares, first with two published reference projects and then with the other projects in its category.
method: Each reference project was graded 3 times with the same pipeline every submission goes through, and the averages are used: 27.63 for the bottom reference and 67.57 for the top. LetsVibe grades on a bell curve: your letter depends on how far your raw score sits above or below the average, measured in standard deviations. Until your category has projects of its own, the bell is set by the references: the average is their midpoint (47.6) and one standard deviation is a quarter of the gap between them (9.985), so the top reference sits two standard deviations above average and the bottom one two below. Each project added to your category shifts the bell toward that category's own average and spread, fully at 30 projects. Two rules tie letters to the references: an A also needs a score at least 75% of the way from the bottom reference to the top one, and a score less than 10% of the way is an F.
